judged_text: Success is checked with `response.statusText !== "OK"` instead of response.ok, but fetch's statusText is the raw reason phrase, which is the empty string for HTTP/2 responses and is not guaranteed to be "OK" for any 2xx. Any environment where the reason phrase is absent or normalized (HTTP/2 via an allowH2 dispatcher, several proxies and edge fetch runtimes return "") turns every successful 200 token refresh into a thrown HttpError 400, breaking all Salesforce auth with no Cal.com-side code change.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new token refresh logic checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)` after `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`. `statusText` is not a reliable indicator of 2xx success (it can be empty or not exactly "OK"), so this can incorrectly throw on successful responses. The diff directly introduces this behavior, and using `response.ok` / status code would be the correct success check.
